The least dumb fix is to stop swapping the whole table: target just the `tbody` (`hx-target="#trails tbody"` with `hx-select="#trails tbody"`) so the header and column widths stay put. Use `useLayoutEffect` when you need to read or change layout before the browser paints, such as measuring an element and positioning a tooltip, so the user never sees a flicker. Otherwise use `useEffect`, which runs after paint and doesn't block it. `useLayoutEffect` also doesn't run on the server, so it can warn during SSR.

They're different. HTTP/1.1 keep-alive reuses one TCP connection for several requests, but one at a time, so a slow response blocks the ones behind it. HTTP/2 multiplexes many concurrent streams over a single connection, so requests and responses interleave; TCP-level head-of-line blocking still exists, which is what HTTP/3 addresses.
Action: none; I can write up a two-line version for standup if you want.

The double post on Enter is usually the form being submitted twice before the first response comes back. With htmx, `hx-disabled-elt` on the submit button plus `hx-sync="this:drop"` on the form drops the second submit while one is pending; a unique constraint on the model is the server-side backstop.

A Deployment is for interchangeable, stateless pods that can start in any order and be replaced freely. A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable name and ordering, and its own persistent volume that follows it, so you pick it for things like databases or brokers where identity and storage matter.
